comparison: Perfect agreement on C1-C5. Both evaluations find the glycoprotein prediction pipeline and experimental validation compelling and supported. OpenEval emphasizes the convergence of computational and experimental evidence, while peer reviewers describe it as part of a 'suite of methods' with 'compelling evidence.'

Perfect agreement on C6-C10. Both evaluations support the evidence that glycosylation (not protein size) drives infection inhibition. OpenEval highlights the hierarchical Bayesian modeling approach, while peer reviewers explicitly state the authors provide 'compelling evidence' for glycan-mediated energy barriers.

Strong agreement on C11-C15, though OpenEval also includes C39-C40 in this result. Both evaluations support the finding that total glycan content predicts infection resistance. Peer reviewers explicitly note the demonstration of 'total glycan content' responsibility, while OpenEval emphasizes the statistical rigor of spatial exclusion and correlation analyses.

Perfect agreement on C16-C18. Both evaluations support the critical mechanistic distinction that glycoproteins do not prevent virus binding but act post-binding. Peer reviewers explicitly accept this finding as allowing the hypothesis of glycan-mediated barriers, while OpenEval describes it as 'clear experimental evidence.'

Perfect agreement on C19. Both evaluations support the finding that infection inhibition is independent of general endocytosis effects. OpenEval notes the molecular weight dependence for large MUC1 variants, while peer reviewers accept it as supporting evidence for the specific mechanism.

Strong agreement on C20-C22, C48-C51. Both evaluations support the FLIM-FRET biophysical characterization. OpenEval includes C52 and emphasizes the rigorous calibration and technical limitations, while peer reviewers describe it as part of the comprehensive 'suite of methods' with no major concerns. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED; peer reviewers also SUPPORTED.

Divergence in evaluation type on C53-C59. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting that while experimental-computational comparisons are solid (C53-C57), the mechanistic interpretation about conformational restriction (C58-C59) is explicitly speculative and requires validation. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED without raising concerns about the speculative nature of these claims.

Perfect agreement on C23-C31. Both evaluations support the in vitro evidence for glycan-mediated intermolecular repulsion. OpenEval emphasizes the appropriate experimental controls and reasonable geometric assumptions, while peer reviewers explicitly note the demonstration that proteins do not transition to brush regime at used densities.

Perfect agreement on C32-C36. Both evaluations support the super-resolution imaging analysis showing size-dependent protein exclusion. OpenEval highlights the sophisticated simulations and calibration, while peer reviewers explicitly cite the finding of 5 nm effective radius threshold with no major concerns.

Perfect agreement on C60-C65. Both evaluations support the polymer brush theory contextualization and interpretation. OpenEval describes the inference as 'reasonable' given literature comparisons, while peer reviewers accept it as part of the theoretical framework providing 'insight on a biophysical mechanism.'

Significant divergence on C41-C42, C66-C74. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the central mechanistic hypothesis is well-reasoned but explicitly speculative in key elements (C66-C68, C70) and requires additional validation. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the proposed physical mechanism as providing 'compelling evidence' without raising concerns about speculative elements.

Overlap on mechanistic details C66-C74. OpenEval (R11) rates these as UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature requiring validation, while peer reviewers (R12) rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the theoretical framework as compelling without concerns about the speculative mechanistic details.

Strong agreement on C43-C47 (background/context claims). Both evaluations support these literature citations as appropriate. OpenEval describes them as providing 'essential background and motivation,' while peer reviewers implicitly accept relevance by noting the work will be of broad interest to relevant communities.

Partial overlap on C37-C38. OpenEval (R12) groups these background claims with C43-C47 and rates as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers (R11) group C37-C38 with the main mechanistic hypothesis (C39-C42) and rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the experimental claim C38 as part of compelling evidence for the energy barrier model.

Partial overlap on C39-C40. OpenEval (R3) groups these with cellular measurements C11-C15 to support additive, nonspecific effects and rates as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers (R11) group C39-C40 with the broader mechanistic hypothesis and rate as SUPPORTED, emphasizing the energy barrier model.

Minimal overlap on C52 only. OpenEval (R5) includes C52 with FLIM-FRET analysis (C20-C22, C48-C51) as SUPPORTED, noting small glycoproteins inhibit infection supporting interface formation model. Peer reviewers (R7) group C52 with structural analysis (C53-C59) as SUPPORTED without distinguishing the specific mechanistic implication.
